skill.name: ai-agents-architect

skill.summary: Guides architecture decisions for reliable, controllable autonomous AI agents.

content.value_statement: Autonomous agents can fail through poor tool design, weak memory rules, and unclear escalation paths. This skill guides architecture decisions for controllable agents.
actual_capabilities: Designs ReAct-style agent loops with explicit iteration limits.
Plans agent workflows using separate planning and execution phases.
Defines tool registries with schemas, examples, and usage tracking.
Advises on selective memory systems for agent context management.
Structures multi-agent systems only when orchestration adds value.
Identifies debugging, tracing, and evaluation needs for agent behavior.
limitations: Provides architectural guidance, not a complete agent runtime.
Requires the user to supply models, tools, APIs, and deployment context.
Does not verify security properties through live testing by itself.
Needs project-specific constraints before recommending detailed designs.

use_cases.title: Design a Tool-Using Agent
use_cases.description: Create an agent architecture with clear tool schemas, safe invocation rules, and bounded execution loops.

use_cases.title: Plan Multi-Agent Coordination
use_cases.description: Decide when multiple agents are justified and define responsibilities, handoffs, and observability requirements.

use_cases.title: Review Agent Failure Modes
use_cases.description: Find risks in memory, planning, tool errors, logging, and escalation before production deployment.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner Agent Blueprint
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when starting a simple autonomous assistant.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a basic AI agent for [task]. Include its goal, tools, memory needs, loop limits, and when it should ask for help.

prompt_templates.title: Tool Registry Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when defining or improving available tools.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these proposed tools for an AI agent: [tools]. Identify missing schemas, unsafe ambiguity, overload, and better tool boundaries.

prompt_templates.title: Planning Strategy Selection
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when a workflow may need planning before execution.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare ReAct and plan-and-execute designs for [workflow]. Recommend one approach with failure handling, replanning triggers, and observability.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced Multi-Agent Architecture
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this for complex systems with several specialized agents.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a multi-agent architecture for [system]. Define agent roles, handoffs, shared memory, conflict handling, evaluation metrics, and production safeguards.

output_examples.input: Design an agent that triages customer support requests and drafts replies.
output: Recommended architecture: one triage agent with bounded tool access and human approval for sensitive replies.
Core tools: ticket lookup, policy search, draft creation, and escalation request.
Controls: maximum loop count, confidence thresholds, trace logging, and explicit escalation rules.

output_examples.input: Review whether my research workflow needs multiple agents.
output: Use one agent unless source gathering, synthesis, and verification require separate accountability.
If split, assign one researcher, one verifier, and one summarizer with logged handoffs.
Avoid shared mutable memory unless conflict resolution and provenance rules are defined.

output_examples.input: Improve an agent that loops too long and hides tool failures.
output: Add a strict iteration limit and a stuck-state response after repeated failed actions.
Expose tool errors as observations so the agent can choose recovery or escalation.
Track each thought, action, observation, and final decision for debugging.

best_practices: Set clear iteration limits and escalation rules before adding autonomy.
Describe every tool with precise inputs, outputs, examples, and failure modes.
Log planning, actions, observations, and final decisions for review.
anti_patterns: Giving an agent unlimited autonomy without stopping conditions.
Adding many tools when a smaller curated set would work.
Saving all context to memory without retention or relevance rules.

faq.question: What does this skill help design?
faq.answer: It helps design autonomous AI agents that use tools, memory, planning, and orchestration with clear controls.

faq.question: Does it build a complete agent application?
faq.answer: No. It provides architecture guidance and design review, while implementation depends on the user project.

faq.question: Can it help with function calling?
faq.answer: Yes. It can define tool schemas, examples, selection rules, error handling, and usage tracking.

faq.question: When should I use multiple agents?
faq.answer: Use multiple agents when separate roles, verification, or parallel work clearly improve reliability or accountability.

faq.question: How does it address agent safety?
faq.answer: It emphasizes bounded loops, explicit escalation, selective memory, trace logging, and visible tool errors.

faq.answer: Yes. The marketplace metadata lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
